newsitem.title: UK: Europe wholesale groups in tough time, image issue.
newsitem.headline: Europe wholesale groups in tough time, image issue.

text.p: Europe's wholesale sector for consumer goods is going through a tough time and some wholesalers have changed the way they do business as a result, Euromonitor, the consumer markets analyst group, said on Tuesday.
It said in its report "Wholesaling in Europe" that the region's wholesale market was expected to grow by 7.2 percent between 1996 and 2000, compared to 21.2 percent growth between 1991 and 1995.
"There can be little doubt that certain changes have taken place which have had severe adverse effects," Euromonitor said.
It said wholesalers had recently taken initiatives to "meet the needs of suppliers and circumvent the actions of retailers".

That included the creation of buying groups to promote bulk purchasing facilities, the development of own-label brands and pan-European alliances, the establishment of closer links with suppliers, and the pursuit of mergers and acquisitions.

Euromonitor said Europe's wholesale sector was worth $1.7 trillion in 1995 at current prices, against 1.4 trillion in 1991. Industries covered included food, pharmaceuticals, clothing and footwear, household goods, electrical goods and cars.
The report said the wholesale industry was growing much faster in emerging markets.
Wholesale turnover in emerging markets within Europe amounted to only $221 billion in 1995, compared to $1.5 billion in the major Western European markets.
But sales in emerging markets have shot up by 838 percent since 1991, against 7.6 percent in the major markets, Euromonitor said.
It said the "average level of spending" was 50 times higher in major European markets in 1991 than in emerging European markets, but the gap has narrowed.
In 1995 average levels of per capita expenditure were only 6.5 times high in Western Europe than in emerging European markets.
Euromonitor said the grocery sector accounted for 40 percent of the total wholesale turnover in Europe between 1991 and 1995.
That included 51-52 percent of the total in Slovenia, Portugal, Norway and the Netherlands, and 24-25 percent in Ukraine, Ireland and Turkey.
Euromonitor said clothing and footwear would be a difficult market for wholesalers over the period 1995 to 2000 and would lose share of the total wholesaling market.
It said total European turnover in the clothing and footwear sector was expected to increase by only $11 billion, compared with $56 billion in the grocery sector.
Europe's motor vehicles wholesale market is expected to show strong signs of growth in Belgium, Greece, Italy, Norway and Portugal, but to be weak in Britain and Ireland.
But the car wholesale market in more developed emerging markets like Poland and Hungary is expected to expand.

Euromonitor said part of the problem being experienced by European wholesalers was that they were not companies known or recognised by the public. The report said wholesalers needed to revamp their image to change that.
